reads: Three corrections. (1) PAGES: the extract closes on n90 (stamp 94) at «pp. 276-278»; the row cited p.281–286. (2) DATE: the row read 1795-08-18. The Treaty of San Ildefonso — the Franco-Spanish alliance the row itself names — is of August 1796, and the surrounding leaves are 1796 material; the copy is undated and unplaced («Sin fecha ni lugar / Sin firma») and gives only «á 2 de Fructidor (23 de Agosto) y ratificada en 26 del mismo por el consejo de los Ancianos en Paris», so the year is supplied from the treaty's identity, not transcribed from the leaf. (3) CONTENT: the row glossed art. 18 as «mutual navigation rights». It is not — art. 18 provides that England being the only power against whom Spain has direct grievances, the alliance shall operate against her alone during the present war, Spain remaining neutral toward the other powers armed against France. The summary now carries the articles as transcribed (4, 5, 18). ⚠ FOURTH correction, found by an adversarial re-read 2026-09-09: the row's own VERBATIM quotation was mistranscribed. Savage writes «Yldefonso» with a capital Y, joins his words as «yla Republica» and «delos Ancianos», and accents «à 2 de Fructidor». The copy is also a SELECTIVE extract beginning at article 4 (arts. 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 18 only), not the whole treaty. And the row previously glossed art. 5 as «18,000 infantry and 6,000 horse»: the manuscript reads «189 infantes y 69 Caballos». Those are the treaty's real figures abbreviated or miscopied, but the record now carries what Savage wrote, with the discrepancy noted.
